title: How a Lithium-Ion Battery Works in 60 Seconds 🔋⚡ #shorts
description:
Your phone battery works by moving lithium ions back and forth. On discharge, ions travel from the graphite anode through the electrolyte to the cathode, while electrons take the outside path and power your device. Charging pushes them back. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#battery #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Secret
steps.text: Your phone battery is just *lithium ions* moving back and forth between two sides.

steps.label: Inside
steps.text: Two electrodes: a graphite *anode* and a metal oxide *cathode*, soaked in electrolyte.

steps.label: Separator
steps.text: A thin *separator* sits between them. Ions can pass, but electrons are blocked.

steps.label: Discharge
steps.text: When you use your phone, ions move from the anode to the *cathode* through the electrolyte.

steps.label: Power
steps.text: The electrons must take the outside path, and that flow *powers* your device.

steps.label: Charging
steps.text: Plug it in, and the charger pushes ions *back* into the graphite, ready again.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Ions inside, electrons *outside*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
